full_judgment: 8. Khondkar Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned advocate for the plaintiff-appellant, firstly, submitted that the plea of defect of party ought not to have been allowed to he raised because in pursuance of an application of the plaintiff, the contesting defendant supplied better particulars upon which the plaint was amended by adding certain persons and as such he was estopped to raise any such plea of defect of party. It does not appear that the plaintiff raised this objection either in the trial Court or in the Appellate Court. How is it that a specific issue a to non-joinder of parties was allowed to be taken up for decision? Then again in the memo of the First Appeal, there is nothing to show that the plaintiff raised the issue of alleged estoppel. The plaintiff cannot be permitted to take such objection here for the first time which needs inquiry into facts. Mr. Ahmed, however, submitted that the finding as to defect of party was not so much fatal as the finding as to adverse possession was, because the plaintiff is not precluded from bringing a fresh suit for partition upon bringing all the necessary parties on record. He, therefore, pressed this appeal mainly on the ground that the finding as to adverse possession was wrongly made.
